title: SDK iterable contracts: prefetch affinity and temporal cursor semantics PRD
creator: Priya Raman
description:
Problem: Clients across Python/TypeScript/Go need a predictable, memory-bounded, backwards-compatible surface for paging and streaming results that supports prefetching, deterministic resume, and clear downgrade semantics when the server returns a compatible but weaker surface. This PRD defines the iterable contracts, token/cursor semantics, prefetch affinity, and retry/backoff rules so SDKs can implement consistent behaviour and interoperate with runtime fallbacks.

Goals:
- Define a single conceptual model (Iterator + Cursor token) that maps naturally to Python/TS/Go idioms.
- Guarantee deterministic resume: a resume token must allow the SDK to continue an iteration with at-most-duplicate results bounded by a configurable safe-window.
- Bounded client memory and prefetch: default prefetch window to limit in-memory buffering while enabling latency improvements for common patterns.
- Backoff and idempotency: provide guidance for retries that avoid visible duplication for at-least-once semantics where possible and allow opt-in stronger guarantees (exactly-once not required).
- Compatibility & downgrade policy: document how SDKs should behave when server surface changes (e.g., switch from chunked streaming to paged responses).
scope: In-scope: API surface for list/stream endpoints (listTokens, listMessages, long-lived streams), resume tokens format, default prefetch window sizes, client-side backoff and retry headers, and cross-language parity tests.
In-scope: Acceptance criteria and SDK test matrix for Python, TypeScript, and Go implementations.
Out-of-scope: End-to-end server-side kernel selection or runtime batching algorithms (handled by runtime team).
Out-of-scope: Transport-level encryption or KMS integration (handled by Private team).
acceptance_criteria: 1) Language parity: feature flag matrix demonstrates equivalent APIs in Python, TypeScript, and Go with idiomatic iterator/async patterns implemented in each SDK.

2) Resume determinism: provided resume token (+ optional offset within last page) allows the client to resume with at most N duplicated items where N <= prefetch_window (default 3). Tests validate duplicates are contiguous and bounded.

3) Memory bounds: default prefetch window configured to 3 items (sync) / 2 pages (paged streaming) and SDKs expose a configurable parameter; memory usage in benchmarks remains linear with window size.

4) Downgrade resilience: when server returns a 'paged-fallback' envelope instead of stream, SDKs transparently switch to a paged iterator while preserving resume tokens and emitting a deprecation warning; automated tests simulate server downgrade.

5) Retry semantics: SDK obeys 'Idempotency-Key' header semantics for retriable item-level operations; list/stream retries use exponential backoff with jitter and preserve order except where documented.
6) Observability hooks: SDKs emit telemetry points when switching modes, encountering resume failures, or hitting prefetch limits (hooks documented and present in all SDKs).
7) Compatibility matrix: documented compatibility table covering prior SDK versions + server minor changes; migration notes included in release notes.
decisions: Decision 1: Use an opaque resume token (base64-encoded JSON) that includes server-side shard id, sequence cursor, and optional page-offset. Clients treat tokens as opaque but may include a client-side offset to allow a small local rewind for duplicate suppression.

Decision 2: Default prefetch window = 3 items for low-latency iterators; expose an integer knob 'prefetch' for advanced users. Rationale: empirical trade-off between latency and memory across common workloads.

Decision 3: SDKs will adopt an 'affinity' concept: prefetch requests should be routed consistently to the same model/shard when feasible; if the server cannot guarantee affinity, server indicates 'affinity_unavailable' in the resume token and SDK falls back to conservative retry behaviour.

Decision 4: Downgrade policy: server may respond with a 'fallback=paged' envelope. SDKs must preserve resume tokens and convert streaming yields into page-aware iterators; preserve ordering and respect prefetch window semantics.

Decision 5: Backoff & retries: exponential backoff with capped jitter; client retries for transient network errors up to 5 attempts by default. Non-idempotent operations must require explicit 'Idempotency-Key' from caller.
dev_notes: Backend: add optional 'fallback' field to list/stream responses and stable resume-token generation (ENG-2377).
SDK: implement iterator adapters - Python (PEP 525 async iter), TS (AsyncIterable), Go (channel-based iterator) with shared test harness.
Telemetry: emit events 'sdk.stream.mode_switch', 'sdk.stream.resume_fail', 'sdk.stream.prefetch_limit' with consistent schema across SDKs.
test_plan: Unit tests: token roundtrip, resume with offset, prefetch window behaviour, downgrade conversion.
Integration tests: cross-language resume interop where a token generated by server during a TypeScript client session is consumed by Python/Go clients.
Load tests: verify memory usage at prefetch window sizes 1,3,10 and validate latency regressions under load.
Chaos tests: simulate mid-stream server restart and validate client resume semantics and duplication bounds.
comments: 2026-03-10 Priya Raman: Draft PRD posted. Goal is cross-lang parity + deterministic resume. Assigned to Ethan Cole for implementation planning.

2026-03-11 Ethan Cole: Implementer notes - prefer exposing 'IteratorOptions.prefetch' and 'IteratorOptions.resume_safe_window' in SDKs. Raised question about default duplicate bounds; recommended default=3. Added ENG-2377 as dependency for resume token work.

2026-03-11 Marco Delgado (SDK Eng): Review feedback - TS ergonomics look good; ask to confirm memory behavior for Node streaming vs browser. Will prototype using streaming iterator that buffers up to prefetch count.
2026-03-12 Aisha Khatri (Design): UX note - include explicit warning hook when SDK switches from streaming to paged fallback; suggested an opt-out console flag for noisy warnings.
2026-03-12 Ethan Cole: Updated acceptance criteria to include observability hooks and compatibility table requirement. Planning spike in cycle 2026-W12 to validate tokens across languages.
2026-03-12 QA Lead (Jordan Price): Test harness request - please provide a reproducible server fixture that can emit both streaming and paged envelopes and force resume token variations.
